identity_reason: a layout primitive only holds its child at a proportion and has no look of its own to derive
concept: AspectRatio holds a picture, a camera view or a chart window at one of four fixed proportions, so the frame never changes shape while its content loads or changes.

root.why: The frame takes its height from its width, so the space is kept before the content arrives and nothing below it moves.

fill.why: The child fills the frame edge to edge, so a window is never half empty and its size is the frame's, not the picture's.

r-1-1.why: The square suits a speaker cover, a room tile or an avatar, where width and height count the same.

r-4-3.why: The four to three frame suits a still from an older camera or a chart window that needs some height.

r-16-9.why: The sixteen to nine frame suits a video or a doorbell view, which arrive wide and keep that shape.

r-3-2.why: The three to two frame suits a photograph and sits between the square and the wide frame.

corner.why: The optional corner reuses the media radius that windows and number cells already use, so a picture nests in its unit the same way.
